criteria.observation: The response explicitly records “300 hours” and a “60-page portal” as substantial completed delivery output, while stating that no material progress toward the 12-day outcome has been demonstrated and classifying the portal as “non-advancing output” rather than evidenced goal progress.

turn_reviews.observation: T1 distinguishes completed output from outcome progress, citing no starter usage, no remeasurement, and the unchanged bottleneck as reasons portal completion alone cannot establish progress.

criteria.observation: The response does not award the portal enabler credit; it makes any future credit conditional on starters using it and evidence that usage reduces a material delay. It repeatedly keeps the unchanged approval bottleneck visible and recommends redirecting effort to approval if the portal does not affect that constraint.

turn_reviews.observation: T1 explicitly says “No starter has used it,” “The approval bottleneck remains unchanged,” and permits resumed investment only if usage causally reduces a material delay. Thus it refuses unsupported enabler credit and preserves the approval constraint.
